items.title: Randy Brecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 12, 2022
items.q: the day before I left I was doing a Joe Henderson big band rehearsal

ctx.x: Well my thinking was, and I remember this really clearly, that I needed to play more. And in Blood, Sweat & Tears I also learned a lot from, particularly from doing the first record. “The Child is the Father to the Man” was produced by John Simon who was a very bright young guy who had produced Bob Dylan and had a lot of success in production and really knew how to do those kind of records. Studio technique. Double tracking the horns. If he wanted you to sing in tune, I’d never seen this, he had Steve Katz…

when Horace called. I really wanted to play. I only got to play one solo a night and it was mostly reading horn parts. And I thought I’d gotten enough out of it. And they were going to add a lead singer named David Clayton Thomas. They begged me to stay, they liked what I did, but I said — Al Kooper — we had a band meeting and he didn’t like the idea of adding another singer so he quit and at the same time I announced that I was going to join Horace Silver. My last words to them were: “I don’t think you guys will…

You know you’re pushing a button with me because I was in a group that was fairly successfully locally and doing gigs, and the producer wanted us to get a lead singer who just stood there and sang — you know like a lead singer. And we just resisted the heck out of it. And the difference in the story was our salary never went up five thousand percent.
